correctness.rationale: For every fixed strictly positive gamma, D_v and r and either specified Poisson full-reset scheme, independently derived exact Gaussian covariances imply a positive-definite conditional velocity law and the stationary age-mixture density. With t proportional to |x| the position variance is 2 kappa(t-d_j)+O(exp(-gamma t)); Gaussian Laplace bounds localize age with exponentially negligible remote contributions. The reference integral sqrt(pi/r)exp(-|x|sqrt(r/kappa)) has exact first two tilted age moments, proving both order-one offsets and the leading variance with o(1) errors. Its moment-generating function establishes the Gaussian age CLT, while uniform Gaussian regression on the saddle window gives the independent N(sqrt(kappa r),D_v/gamma) velocity law; exponential marginal tails supply the independent threshold overshoot. The proof distinguishes conditioned-on-density sampling from crossing-time sampling. The standalone checker passed its actual bounded tests but is not used to prove infinity-range claims.

The new proof is a nontrivial conditional Laplace analysis, not a rebranding of the existing marginal tails. Priority remains qualified by possible implicit coverage under broader general conditional-limit results.

RESULT.md: exact conditional age and velocity laws and proof
value.rationale: A large displacement in a nominally zero-mean stationary inertial particle selects a positive effective velocity, not a centered Maxwellian, and a reset age of order displacement with Gaussian square-root fluctuations. Two reset protocols have the same selected kinetic law but their mean conditional ages differ by exactly 1/(2 gamma); the threshold overshoot adds a measurable independent exponential coordinate. These are natural conditional observables tied to how extreme events are realized, unavailable from the already known marginal tail prefactors alone. The result directly informs interpretation of rare-displacement experiments and provides a scheme discriminator, rather than an arbitrary parameter exercise.
